title: Find Median from Data Stream
summary: Start with an empty number stream.

contractDetails.constraints: Inserted numbers are integers in [−100,000, 100,000]. At most 50,000 operations occur. Each median query follows at least one insertion. Numeric results within 0.00001 of the true median are accepted.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare each numeric result in operation order with an absolute tolerance of 0.00001.

statement: Start with an empty number stream. AddNum inserts one integer. FindMedian returns the middle value in sorted order, or the arithmetic mean of the two middle values if the count is even. The fixture uses [0,value] for addNum and [1] for findMedian and collects only median results.

examples.explanation: The two-item median is the mean of 4 and 7.
Both copies of 2 affect the rank.

constraints: Inserted numbers are integers in [−100,000, 100,000]. At most 50,000 operations occur. Each median query follows at least one insertion. Numeric results within 0.00001 of the true median are accepted.
hints: Conceptual: The median is at the boundary between the lower and upper halves.
Directional: Keep the lower half in a max heap and the upper half in a min heap.
Implementation: Rebalance after every insertion so the lower half has the same number of items as the upper half or one extra. Read the relevant heap tops.
complexityAnalysis: O(log(n+1)) time per insertion, O(1) per query and O(n) space for n inserted values.
